In the figure, Australia is located on the right side, in the area east of 90°E. Then reason: the text states that in this season the isotherms of the North American continent protrude southward, indicating that the Northern Hemisphere is in winter and the Southern Hemisphere is in summer. Combined with the trend of the morning-evening line MN in the figure, it can be judged that point N is located on the evening line, so EP, namely the 0° meridian, has local time 18:00. A local time difference of 6 hours corresponds to a longitude difference of 90°, so the 0:00 meridian is 90°E. From east of 90°E to near 180° belongs to the new day, and Australia is east of 90°E; while Brazil is located in the Western Hemisphere, in another date range west of 90°E. Therefore, at the time shown in the figure, Australia and Brazil are not on the same day.
